KakuKaku looks up Japanese text from your screen. It is a continuation of Kaku by 0xbad1d3a5 (github.com/0xbad1d3a5/Kaku) and is not endorsed by its author. It works offline and collects no data.

Dictionary data
JMdict and KANJIDIC2 are the property of the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (EDRDG) and are used under its licence (CC BY-SA 4.0), www.edrdg.org/edrdg/licence.html. The built-in dictionary is derived from them.

Conjugation rules
The deinflection rules (deinflect.dat) come from Rikaichan by Jonathan Zarate. Rikaichan is licensed under the GNU General Public License (version 2 or later); this file is not covered by the BSD licence below and keeps its original terms.

Libraries
Google ML Kit text recognition (Google terms), Tesseract OCR (Apache License 2.0) through Tesseract4Android (Apache License 2.0) with the Japanese language data jpn and jpn_vert of the tessdata project (Apache License 2.0), AndroidX and Material Components, Gson (Apache License 2.0), ORMLite (ISC licence).

Press Start (1). Android asks you to allow display over other apps and screen capture; both are needed to show the box and read the text under it. Everything stays on your device.
A box (1) floats over every app. Drag it over the Japanese text. To resize it, drag its bottom-right corner (2).
Double-tap the box. At the top appear the characters it found (1) and below them the dictionary entries (2). Tap another character to look up from there; tap beside the card or swipe up to close it.

If a character was read wrongly, press it and drag down (1): lookalikes (2) appear. Release over one to swap it. Drag up-left to edit or delete the character instead, and long-press the card to copy the whole text.
In any app, select Japanese text (1) and choose KakuKaku (2) from the menu or from Share. No box needed.
The notification (1) turns on Instant mode (scan as soon as you release the box), turns on Image Filter, and pauses KakuKaku.
With Filter on, the box adds a black and white filter (1). Press and hold the box and slide your finger left or right (2) to change the threshold.
No saved words yet. Tap the list icon next to a definition to save it here.
Remove all %1$d saved words? This cannot be undone.
{sentence}: sentence of the source text that has the term
{furigana-plain}: term with furigana in brackets, 日本語[にほんご]
{cloze-body}: the term as it appeared in the text (inflected)
{pitch-accent-positions}: pitch accent downstep position as a number
{writing}: term deinflected, written as it appeared in the text
{writing-furigana}: the written form with furigana (HTML ruby)
{writing-furigana-plain}: the written form with furigana in brackets
AnkiDroid is not installed. Install it to send terms to Anki.
KakuKaku needs your permission to add cards to AnkiDroid.
Nothing to choose from. Open AnkiDroid once and try again.
Write text and markers like {expression} or {reading}; leave a field empty to keep it empty. The grey line shows an example.
Write these markers in a field. Each is replaced by the information about the term you add. Text around them stays as typed.
Next to each definition, adds the term to AnkiDroid.
Word list icon in the popup
Next to each definition, saves the term to the word list.
Choose a deck and a note type for Anki first
The sentence of the text the term is in, from the source content.
The term in dictionary form, for example 食べる for 食べました.
The term in kana: たべる.
The term with its reading over the kanji, as HTML ruby: 食べる with た above 食.
The term with its reading in brackets: 食[た]べる. For Anki fields that use {{furigana:…}}.
The term as it appeared in the text, inflected: 食べました.
The dictionary definitions, as a numbered list with parts of speech.
The pitch accent downstep notation from the pitch accent dictionary: [2]. Empty without one.
The pitch accent downstep positions as numbers: 2, 0. Empty without a pitch accent dictionary.
The term deinflected but written the way it was in the text: 喰べる if the text had 喰べた, たべる if it had たべた.
The written form with its reading over the kanji, as HTML ruby.
The written form with its reading in brackets.
Tesseract (older, slower; shows several choices per character)
Joins lines of selected or scanned text into one. Turn off to keep each line break, which ends a word lookup.
Leaves out the small reading above kanji, in scanned and in selected text. Turn off if it ever removes real text.

KakuKaku does not include pitch accent data. Import a pitch accent dictionary in Yomitan format (a .zip with term_meta_bank_N.json files), for example one from the Yomitan wiki. The accent is shown after the reading, like 猫 (ねこ) [1].

KakuKaku does not include frequency data. Import a frequency dictionary in Yomitan format (a .zip with term_meta_bank_N.json files), for example JPDB or BCCWJ from the Yomitan wiki. Of two results that match the same text, the more common word is then shown first.
JMdict is updated almost daily. Download JMdict_english.zip, then import it here to replace the old copy.

Import dictionaries in Yomitan format: a .zip file (not unpacked) with index.json and term_bank_N.json or kanji_bank_N.json files. Words are looked up in one dictionary at a time. Kanji details always come from the built-in dictionary.
Find more dictionaries on the Yomitan wiki, for example Jitendex, JMdict, JMnedict, KANJIDIC and Wiktionary.
Delete \"%1$s\"? You can import it again later.
Press Start to begin. Android will ask for permission to show over other apps and to capture your screen.
Display over other apps is off

KakuKaku needs this permission to show the capture box. If the switch is greyed out or turns itself off, Android is restricting an app installed from a browser or file manager.\n\nOpen the app info, tap the ⋮ menu in the top-right corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then press Start again. (The menu entry appears after you have tried to enable the permission once.)
Press Start first to grant the overlay permission
